findings.title: L1's absolute accuracy depends on its coarse default mesh offsetting its model error, and L1 does not converge as the mesh is refined
findings.detail: L1 is below L2_inf on all 90 layouts, by 5.1–14.4% (mean -9.7%), so MAPE is simply the size of this bias. Refining the L1 mesh moves it further away from the reference: MAPE is 0.097, 0.101, 0.111 and 0.1215 at hmax 4, 2, 1 and 0.5 mm. At 0.5 mm the point value alone already exceeds the A4 threshold of 0.12. The refinement steps do not contract: the median step is -0.42%, -1.12% and -1.19%, so the 1→0.5 mm step is 1.03 times the 2→1 mm step, where a converging scheme would give about 0.25–0.5. This contradicts the model.py docstring's Richardson estimate (order p = 1..2, default mesh '+2.3..+5.4 % above the mesh-converged L1'). The mesh-converged L1 is therefore unknown and is at least 12% low. A4 passes only because the 4 mm mesh's positive discretisation bias partly cancels a larger negative model bias. The ranking claim survives, because Spearman rises from 0.9958 to 0.9974 as the mesh is refined, but L1 is only defined by its 4 mm default mesh, not by a converged model.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from e002_rows.json: mesh 4/2/1/0.5 mm gives rho 0.99585/0.99615/0.99700/0.99742 and MAPE 0.0972/0.1007/0.1109/0.1215; 100% of layouts have L1 < L2_inf; median step ratios 2.36 and 1.03.
findings.suggested_check: Record hmax = 4 mm as part of the L1 model definition in the claim, and diagnose the -10% bias (it is consistent with the plane-facing-face-only current layer) before quoting absolute L1 numbers.

findings.title: L1 cannot reliably order layouts whose loop inductances differ by less than about 5%
findings.detail: Rho = 0.996 comes mostly from the large spread across families and die counts (CV of L2_inf 0.36; side_by_side 3.5–5.9 nH against 7.3–13.2 nH for the other families). Within one (family, dies) stratum the mean Spearman is 0.92 and the minimum is 0.77 (n = 6 each). Pairs of layouts that the reference puts within 2% of each other are ordered wrongly 37.5% of the time, close to a coin flip; pairs within 5% are wrong 22.6% of the time, and every misordered pair is within 4.4%. The scatter of L1's per-layout error is about 2% (sd within a die count). An optimizer refining a derivative re-layout near its optimum works exactly in this <5% regime.
findings.evidence: Pairwise analysis over 4005 pairs: 89 misordered (Kendall tau 0.956). Same-stratum pairs: 18 of 225 misordered. Within-family rho: interleaved 0.988, side_by_side 0.979, u_shaped 0.995.
findings.suggested_check: Limit the claim to 'orders layouts whose L differs by more than about 5%', or report the misordering rate as a function of the reference gap.

findings.title: L1's bias depends on die count and family, so it overstates the benefit of adding dies
findings.detail: The signed L1 error grows from -7.8% at 2 dies to -10.6% at 6 dies, and varies by family from -7.5% (u_shaped) to -11.7% (side_by_side). As a result L1 overstates how much L falls from 2 to 6 dies: in side_by_side L1 gives L(6)/L(2) = 0.768 against 0.803 from L2. The residual correlates with die count (resid_spearman_dies -0.33, -0.47 at the fine mesh; both CIs exclude 0). Interleaved and u_shaped overlap in L and differ in bias by about 2.5%, so close cross-family comparisons will lean towards interleaved.
findings.suggested_check: Report die-count trade-off conclusions with this bias stated, or check them against L2.

findings.title: Scope says 'DBC or AMB', but every tested layout uses one default DBC stack from one 3-family generator
findings.detail: generate/halfbridge.py builds every layout with default_dbc_stack(). No AMB stack and no alternative ceramic or copper thickness was sampled. L1's bias depends on the Cu-to-plane gap (bottom-face current layer, image plane fixed at the backside-Cu top face), so the size of the bias, and its spread across layouts, could change with a different stack. The evidence covers only this stack and the three generated topologies.
findings.evidence: halfbridge.py line 109: stack = default_dbc_stack(); no stack parameter in generate_layouts.
findings.suggested_check: Narrow the scope to the default DBC stack, or add an AMB stratum.

findings.title: The E002 reference is converged only in lateral refinement
findings.detail: The L2 refinement ladder refines lateral cells only. Thickness layers (10/6/6) and wire filaments are the same at every level, so the in-run l2_converged check does not cover them. Their sensitivity was measured outside the run on one or two layouts: -0.043% for +2 layers, -0.18% for doubled layers graded at 20 MHz, +0.02% for wire filaments. These are small enough not to threaten the ranking, but they are not part of the evidence for the 'converged reference' wording.
findings.evidence: l2_layout.py docstring lines 49-56; research/l2_layout_vm/solve_s7_d2_r1{,_layers_x2_f20}.json: 11.0292 vs 11.0095 nH; docs/notes/o001-l2-layout-cost.md line 189.
findings.suggested_check: Optional: add one vertical-refinement solve per family to a future E002-class run.

findings.title: Timing evidence was measured at a different commit, on unpinned Apple silicon, and saved no per-call data
findings.detail: E003 ran at commit 4c8cf3e on 2026-10-12, while E002 ran at 59d3ce7. This snapshot has a single commit, so the L1 code used for timing cannot be confirmed from git. E003 saved no artifacts (no per-call times or L values), so its median cannot be recomputed. The machine was an Apple M5 without core pinning. My local rerun covers the gap: at this commit L1 reproduces E002's L1 values to 1.5e-12 and gives p50 = 17.9 ms. The ≤ 50 ms claim holds on Apple silicon but is not shown for other CPUs (for example the x86 machines used for E002).
findings.evidence: E003 result.json: provenance git_commit 4c8cf3e, artifacts []; E002 git_commit 59d3ce7.
findings.suggested_check: Save per-call timings and the L1 source hash in future E003 runs.

findings.title: The evaluator never reports 'not_satisfied' for CI-based fail checks
findings.detail: In evaluate.judge with as_fail=True, the outcome is either 'satisfied' or 'undetermined'. So K1 (rho CI [0.990, 0.998] against a kill at < 0.80) and K2 (MAPE CI [0.092, 0.102] against a kill at > 0.20) show as 'undetermined' even though both CIs clearly rule out the kill. This is cosmetic and does not affect PASS, because a kill can still be reported as 'satisfied'.
findings.suggested_check: Return not_satisfied when the opposite CI bound also fails the kill comparator.

independent_checks_performed: Recomputed Spearman rho (0.99585) and MAPE (0.0972) from e002_rows.json using Richardson-extrapolated L2 (r_hat = 0.5836); both match result.json

Read the evaluator's judge() logic and checked the bound each A/K criterion used against the objective.yaml uncertainty settings
Checked that the L2 layout solver imports no L1 code, and reviewed the L2 docstring and research files for vertical and wire-filament mesh sensitivity
Checked the layout generator for stack variation: only the default DBC stack is used
caveats: The claim is supported for ranking layouts whose loop inductances differ by more than about 5%. Below that, L1 misorders 23–38% of pairs.
Supported only for the generator's three families on the single default DBC stack; AMB substrates and other stack thicknesses are untested.
The L1 'model' must include its 4 mm default mesh. L1 does not converge on refinement, and its absolute values are about 10% low; A4 (MAPE ≤ 12%) would fail at hmax 0.5 mm.
L1 has a bias that grows with die count, so it overstates the inductance benefit of adding dies by about 2–3.5 percentage points.
The 50 ms timing is shown on Apple silicon (M5, unpinned), both in E003 and in my rerun; it is not shown on other CPUs.
Running `uv run` created an untracked .venv in the worktree; no tracked files were modified. My scratch analysis ran as inline python -c commands, because file writes to /tmp were blocked.
